display_title: 21-4-1 水葫芦在肯尼亚蔓延带来的难题与益处

sentences.en: Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes), an aquatic plant native to South America, first appeared in countries in Africa in the early 1900s.
sentences.zh: 水葫芦（学名 Eichhornia crassipes）是一种原产南美洲的水生植物，20世纪初首次出现在非洲一些国家。

sentences.en: Scientists there called it the 'world's worst aquatic weed', after it spread from the southernmost tip of Africa in the early 1900s and started obstructing major dams and rivers.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初，水葫芦从非洲最南端向外扩散，开始堵塞主要的水坝和河道，当地科学家因此称它为“世界上最糟糕的水生杂草”。

sentences.en: In east Africa the plant arrived with Belgian colonists in Rwanda, who liked the look of its glossy leaves and delicate purple flowers floating in their ponds.
sentences.zh: 在东非，水葫芦是随比利时殖民者进入卢旺达的。殖民者喜欢看到它油亮的叶片和娇嫩的紫花漂在自家池塘里的模样。

sentences.en: But by the 1980s, it had 'escaped' out of the country via the Kagera river and made its way downstream to Lake Victoria.
sentences.zh: 但到20世纪80年代，它已沿卡盖拉河“逃”出了卢旺达，顺流进入维多利亚湖。

sentences.en: There, with no natural predators and perfect temperature conditions, the plant began spreading in the open water, blocking fishing routes and providing a new habitat for disease-carrying mosquitoes.
sentences.zh: 湖里没有它的天敌，温度又恰到好处，水葫芦便开始在开阔水面上蔓延，堵住渔船航道，并为传播疾病的蚊子提供了新的栖息地。

sentences.en: For the women who smoke fish from the lake to sell it has meant declining income, as the boats that once brought the fish to shore by the hundreds struggle to navigate through the mass of plants.
sentences.zh: 对靠熏制湖鱼出售的妇女而言，水葫芦带来了收入下降：那些过去能把成百条鱼运到岸边的船，如今挤在大片水葫芦中，通行十分困难。

sentences.en: But water hyacinth isn't their only headache.
sentences.zh: 但让她们头疼的还不止水葫芦。

sentences.en: In order to smoke the fish that they buy, they must gather huge quantities of firewood, sometimes walking as far as 10km each way to collect enough to complete their work.
sentences.zh: 要把买来的鱼熏好，她们得捡回大量柴火，有时单程就得走上足足10公里，才能凑够干活用的柴。

sentences.en: And each day as they cook, they breathe in the thick, grey smoke.
sentences.zh: 每天做饭时，她们都在吸入浓厚的灰烟。

sentences.en: About three out of four families in Kenya depend on wood or charcoal to cook their daily meals, and the rate is even higher in rural areas, Kenya's latest demographic and health survey shows.
sentences.zh: 肯尼亚最近一次人口与健康调查显示，每四户家庭中约有三户依靠木柴或木炭烹制日常饭食，在农村地区，这一比例还要高。

sentences.en: Using solid fuels like these for cooking increases indoor pollution.
sentences.zh: 用这类固体燃料做饭会加重室内污染。

sentences.en: The World Health Organization estimates that about 14,300 Kenyans die annually as a result of indoor air pollution – most of which is caused by cooking and heating sources.
sentences.zh: 世界卫生组织估计，肯尼亚每年约有14,300人死亡，原因是室内空气污染，而这些污染主要来自做饭和取暖。

sentences.en: Some years ago, on the shores of Lake Victoria, huge piles of water hyacinth that villagers had taken out of the water in an attempt to clear it were a common sight.
sentences.zh: 几年前，维多利亚湖岸边常见一大堆一大堆的水葫芦，那是村民为了清理水域而从湖里捞上来的。

sentences.en: But buried in those decaying waxy leaves was a renewable energy gold mine.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些正在腐烂、表面带蜡质的叶片里，却埋藏着一座可再生能源的“金矿”。

sentences.en: It turns out the floating plant isn't just good at spreading – its foliage also contains a high ratio of carbon to nitrogen.
sentences.zh: 原来，这种漂浮植物的长处不只是蔓延得快，它的叶片还具有很高的碳氮比。

sentences.en: It's a magic combination that has captivated researchers' imaginations since as early as the 1980s when, across the world, they began to explore its potential as a biofuel.
sentences.zh: 这种奇妙的组合早在20世纪80年代就激起了研究者的想象力。当时，世界各地的研究人员开始探索将它用作生物燃料的潜力。

sentences.en: Just about 4kg of the dried plant would be enough to cater for a large family's daily energy needs, early research predicted.
sentences.zh: 早期研究预测，只需大约4千克晒干的水葫芦，就足以满足一个大家庭一天的能源需求。

sentences.en: In 2014, Nigerian academics announced they had got better yields of biofuel gas when they mixed the plant with chicken manure.
sentences.zh: 2014年，尼日利亚学者宣布，他们把水葫芦与鸡粪混合后，获得了更高的生物燃气产量。

sentences.en: A few years later, Kenyan scientists confirmed what their Nigerian peers and others had already found: manure worked to improve the process of converting the weed into gas.
sentences.zh: 几年后，肯尼亚科学家证实了尼日利亚同行和其他研究者此前的发现：添加畜禽粪便确实有助于改善将这种杂草转化为燃气的过程。

sentences.en: In 2018, the technology came to a village on the shore of Lake Victoria, called Dunga.
sentences.zh: 2018年，这项技术传到了维多利亚湖岸边一个叫东加的村庄。

sentences.en: The project promised a two-for-one solution to the dual menaces of the water hyacinth and dependence on firewood.
sentences.zh: 这个项目有望一举解决两项威胁：水葫芦泛滥，以及当地人对柴火的依赖。

sentences.en: The community received a pair of donated biogas digesters – machines that would transform a mix of water hyacinth and cow dung into biogas for cooking.
sentences.zh: 村里获赠两台沼气消化器，能将水葫芦和牛粪的混合物转化成做饭用的沼气。

sentences.en: The digesters work a bit like a stomach.
sentences.zh: 消化器的工作方式有点像胃。

sentences.en: The mixture goes in one end – think of it as a mouth – and over the next 20 to 30 days, it goes through a fermentation process and breaks down, giving off gas that comes out the other end.
sentences.zh: 混合物从一端进入，可以把这一端看作嘴巴。在接下来的20至30天里，混合物发酵、分解，释放出的气体从另一端排出。

sentences.en: From there, the clean-burning gas is passed through pipes to the point of use, just like traditional domestic gas.
sentences.zh: 从那里开始，这种燃烧清洁的气体便和传统家用燃气一样，通过管道输送到使用地点。

sentences.en: In Dunga, the machines produce enough gas to serve about 60% of the village's population.
sentences.zh: 在东加，这两台机器产出的燃气足以供全村大约60%的居民使用。

sentences.en: It is used in domestic stoves and for other household tasks such as purifying water and incubating chicks.
sentences.zh: 这种沼气既供家用炉灶使用，也用来净化水、孵小鸡等。

sentences.en: The project is testing whether biogas can provide an effective alternative to firewood and charcoal in rural Kenyan communities.
sentences.zh: 项目正在检验，沼气能否在肯尼亚农村社区有效替代木柴和木炭。

sentences.en: Results indicate that the programme seems to be working.
sentences.zh: 结果表明，这个项目似乎正在奏效。

sentences.en: The women who smoke the lake fish are already getting sick less often.
sentences.zh: 现在，熏制湖鱼的妇女生病的次数已经减少了。

sentences.en: Besides, they don't have to devote a lot of time every day to gathering firewood, which is a great relief.
sentences.zh: 此外，她们再也不必每天花大量时间拾柴，这让她们轻松了许多。

sentences.en: As a result, they're able to make more money for their families from other enterprises.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，她们就有余力从事其他营生，为家人多挣些钱。

sentences.en: Kanyiva Muindi is an epidemiologist and air pollution research fellow at the African Population and Health Research Centre in Nairobi.
sentences.zh: 卡尼瓦·穆因迪是内罗毕非洲人口与健康研究中心的流行病学家，也是空气污染研究员。

sentences.en: She says families who switch to the smokeless cooking method could expect fewer respiratory diseases.
sentences.zh: 她说，改用这种无烟烹饪方式的家庭有望减少呼吸系统疾病。

sentences.en: Women, young girls and children are particularly vulnerable because they are the ones who cook in the kitchen or outside over fires.
sentences.zh: 妇女、女孩和儿童尤其容易受害，因为在厨房或户外生火做饭的正是他们。

sentences.en: How much better the biogas stoves will be for the community's health still needs more research, says Dominic Kahumbu Wanjihia, Biogas International's chief executive.
sentences.zh: 国际沼气公司首席执行官多米尼克·卡洪布·万吉希亚说，沼气炉究竟能给社区居民的健康带来多大改善，还需要更多研究。

sentences.en: But unless the price of the machines drops, it's pretty clear that most communities will never be able to afford any, since they sell for about $750.
sentences.zh: 不过，这些设备每台约售750美元。显然，除非价格下降，否则大多数社区永远也买不起哪怕一台。

sentences.en: Kanyiva says affordability is a challenge worth addressing, given the huge health and environmental dangers posed by 'dirty' fuels such as wood, charcoal and kerosene.
sentences.zh: 卡尼瓦说，木柴、木炭、煤油等“不清洁”燃料会给健康和环境带来极大危险，因此，让人们用得起沼气这个难题值得设法解决。

sentences.en: If biogas could become affordable on a large scale, she says it 'would be life-changing for millions on the African continent and beyond'.
sentences.zh: 她说，如果能让广大民众都用得起沼气，那“将会改变非洲大陆乃至其他地区数百万人的生活”。
